subject: Geopolitics
title: The Sykes-Picot Legacy
description: A fast breakdown of The Sykes-Picot Legacy for builders.

hook.text: In 1916 a British and a French diplomat drew lines across the Middle East in secret. The region still bleeds.

buildup.text: Sykes-Picot split Ottoman lands into zones. Iraq combined Sunnis, Shia, and Kurds who never chose to coexist.

discovery.text: Borders that ignore identity create states that must repress to survive. Saddam's Iraq was the result.

twist.text: ISIS declared Sykes-Picot dead in 2014, erasing the Iraq–Syria border. The century-old map still provokes.

climax.text: Kurdish independence, Lebanese fragmentation, and Iraqi sectarianism all stem from those secret lines.

punchline.text: Two men, one map, a century of war.

quiz.question: What did the Sykes-Picot Agreement do?
options: Granted independence to Middle Eastern nations
Secretly divided Ottoman lands between Britain and France
